text:
nina: heads up — our bulk rewrap job hit KMS throttling across multiple keys during the last run (job=rw-2026-03-09-17, ~2M objects). Seeing AWS KMS Throttling and GCP ResourceExhausted. sample error: 
```
ERROR rewrap worker: key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd1234 - ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded (Retryable)
stack: .../rewrap/worker.go:142
```
I paused the job. Need a plan for safe resume + audit trail.

sam: thanks, nina. good catch. quick Qs: are we rewrapping by DEK per-object or doing batch DEK wrap with per-key concurrency?

nina: DEK-per-object. Workers pull messages from rewrap-sqs. Current setup: 100 parallel workers per region + no per-key limiter. That probably hammered a handful of hot CMKs.

oliver: yep, hot-key problem. For large migrations we should:
- add per-CMK token-bucket (permits/sec)
- fall back to local envelope key for short-term buffering (wrap locally, queue KMS rewrap async)
- emit an audit event for each object rewrap with job_id + old_key_id + new_key_id + checksum

sam: agree. also: exponential backoff + jitter on 429s, and cap max concurrency per key to ~5 (tuneable). Example backoff snippet we use:
```
backoff = min(30s, base * 2^attempt) + rand(0, 250ms)
```
And track per-key error rate metric: rewrap.kms_errors{key_id}.

jp: we should also leverage KMS key policies / IAM to limit parallel usage from a single principal? maybe split rewrap principals across workers (rewrap-role-1..N) to avoid a single principal hitting account-level quotas.

nina: good point. AWS has per-account KMS limits too. splitting principals helped in a past migration but increases complexity for audit mapping. We need to map principal -> job_id in audit logs.

oliver: Also consider two-phase rewrap:
1) quick local wrap: generate a new local-wrapped-DEK and push object, mark as 'pending-kms'
2) background rewrap-by-key: one controlled worker per-CMK rewraps queued pending-kms items and updates audit when done
This reduces tail latency for user requests and centralizes KMS calls.

rewrap-bot: Job rw-2026-03-09-17 paused at 2026-03-09T17:12:04Z due to repeated ThrottlingException (aws:kms). 1,842,371 processed, 157,629 remaining.

sam: operationally we should:
- implement per-key rate limiter (token bucket) in worker pool
- add per-key 'hot' flag that reduces concurrency to 1 for 10m on repeated 429s
- increase visibility: expose in console: rewrap job progress + per-key QPS and 429 rate

nina: for audit: make sure every object emit includes prev_kid, new_kid, job_id, worker_id, retry_count, and a sha256 of the plaintext DEK (or HMAC) so we can verify integrity without storing plaintext. retention: keep these events for 90 days then archive.

jp: note on GCP KMS: automatic retry quotas are a bit different — GCP may return ResourceExhausted but doesn't expose per-key QPS easily. For GCP we can shard by key-locations and implement small per-key delays.

oliver: error recovery: if a key rewrap permanently fails (AccessDenied or NotFound), route to "manual-review" queue and mark object as failed in audit. For retryable errors, exponential backoff with capped attempts (e.g., 7 attempts) then escalate.

nina: timeline? I can spike the token-bucket change and per-key metrics tomorrow. Who can own console surface for rewrap job?

sam: I can PR a metrics dashboard (Grafana) and add a per-job panel. I'll also add rewrap.kms_429_rate and rewrap.kms_qps per key.

jp: I'll work on IAM split/principal design — short doc outlining tradeoffs and how to tag principal -> job.

rewrap-bot: Job rw-2026-03-09-17 resume_candidate queued (will require operator approval). current remaining: 157,629

oliver: small playbook for restart:
1) enable token-bucket defaults: 5 qps per CMK
2) set worker concurrency global -> 200, but per-key enforced
3) resume on low-traffic window (00:00-04:00 PT)
4) watch rewrap.kms_429_rate and pause automatically if >1% sustained for 5m

nina: perfect. I'll draft runbook and add a CLI to resume with flags: --job rw-... --dry-run --concurrency=200 --per-key-qps=5

sec-ci-bot: :white_check_mark: rw-2026-03-09-17 dry-run completed (sample 100 objs) — no KMS 429s at per-key-qps=5.

sam: nice. next steps: PR token-bucket lib, dashboard, runbook, and a short postmortem explaining why per-key limits were missing initially. assign owners?

nina: owners: sam (dashboard + metrics) / jp (IAM + principal split) / oliver (worker changes + token-bucket lib) / nina (runbook + audit schema). target: get changes staged by end of next week and run a controlled resume the following maintenance window.

oliver: :thumbsup: I'll also add a small simulation harness to estimate total wall-time at different per-key qps settings so we can pick defaults.

nina: thanks all — leaving the thread open for updates. if anyone sees other causes (network throttles, KMS regional outages), drop logs here.
